feature_results.rationale: Claude Code answers natural-language questions about code across the whole repository, but it does NOT build a semantic/embedding index (RAG over code). Anthropic documents an intentional agentic-search design: Claude navigates on demand using file reads, grep/glob and LSP symbol lookups, driven by the model's understanding of the query, and explicitly declines codebase indexing. This delivers meaning-based, repository-wide retrieval as an outcome, but not via the semantic index / codebase indexing / RAG mechanism the feature centrally describes, and it is more than plain substring/regex alone. Because the core indexing mechanism is deliberately absent while meaning-based whole-repo retrieval is nonetheless achieved through agentic exploration, the strict judgment is partial rather than has or not_found.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code finds this approach more effective and flexible than full codebase indexing.

constraints.description: Claude Code maintains no embedding pipeline or persistent semantic/centralized index; codebase retrieval is performed by live agentic exploration (file reads, grep/glob, LSP symbol search) rather than meaning-based index retrieval. An external code-search/RAG index can only be added by exposing it as an MCP tool.

feature_results.rationale: Anthropic's official Claude Code data-usage documentation describes concrete, customer-facing controls over training use and data retention. Under commercial terms (Team, Enterprise, API, third-party platforms, Claude Gov) code and prompts sent to Claude Code are not used to train models by default unless the customer chooses to opt in (e.g., the Development Partner Program), and Enterprise/commercial organizations can configure custom data retention controls and zero-data-retention arrangements. This exceeds generic privacy-policy language and constitutes actionable opt-out/no-training controls.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms, unless the customer has chosen to provide their data to us for model improvement.

constraints.description: The no-training default applies under commercial terms (Team, Enterprise, API, third-party platforms). Configurable custom data retention controls and zero-data-retention arrangements are positioned for Enterprise/commercial organizations rather than for all consumer tiers.

constraints.description: Inline per-edit diff review with accept/reject is the default (Manual) behavior; other permission modes such as acceptEdits or bypassPermissions auto-approve edits and defer or skip the inline review step.

feature_results.rationale: No official Anthropic source describes as-you-type ghost-text or inline code suggestions generated in an editor without an explicit prompt. Claude Code is an agent-driven CLI/IDE tool; the overview explicitly positions it as a shift away from autocomplete-based assistants (it works 'through natural language commands'). The only autocomplete-like features found in the changelog are slash-command autocomplete and bash-mode history tab completion, which are command-UI conveniences, not inline completion of source code as defined by this feature. Documentation, product page, changelog, and pricing were all checked with no supporting statement.

feature_results.rationale: Anthropic documents explicit context-scale handling mechanisms for Claude Code beyond a raw model window: automatic compaction summarizes work into a new context window near the limit, extended (1M-token) context windows are supported on newer models, and agentic search plus subagent delegation keep large-codebase exploration out of the main context. These are codebase/session-specific handling mechanisms, satisfying the has_criteria.

evidence.excerpt: Claude Code also auto-compacts when you get close to the limit, so you will rarely hit a hard wall.
When you're nearing the end of the context window, the task you've been working on is automatically summarized into a smaller description and the model continues the work in a new context window.

constraints.description: The extended 1M-token context window is available only on specific newer models; other models rely on the standard window plus auto-compaction and manual /compact and /clear controls.

feature_results.rationale: Official Claude Code enterprise deployment documentation states that customers can run Claude Code against models in their own existing Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI (and Microsoft Foundry) instances within their existing VPC, integrating with their own IAM/logging, so data stays within the customer's control rather than only Anthropic's shared cloud. This matches the definition's 'dedicated private cloud instance rather than only the vendor's shared cloud' and satisfies the has criteria. Note this is a customer-cloud/private-VPC deployment via cloud-provider integrations, not a fully air-gapped self-hosting of the model weights on the customer's own hardware.

feature_results.rationale: Claude Code documents CLAUDE.md files as persistent, project-scoped instructions written once and loaded automatically at the start of every session (with user, project and organization scopes concatenated by specificity), plus an Auto memory system that accumulates project knowledge across sessions without manual re-entry. This is a documented mechanism that persists guidance across sessions and is applied automatically, fully meeting the has_criteria.

constraints.description: CLAUDE.md files are loaded into the context window at the start of every session and consume tokens; very large memory files can reduce instruction adherence, so path-scoped rules or trimming are recommended.

use_cases.title: Governed enterprise rollout with isolation and data controls
use_cases.description: A platform team deploys Claude Code across the organization with SSO and role-based access, runs agent commands inside OS-level sandboxes, keeps data in their own cloud via Bedrock/Vertex, and relies on the no-training-by-default commercial terms.
use_cases.rationale: Enterprise SSO/RBAC, sandboxed execution, customer-cloud private deployment, and training opt-out controls are each individually supported features that combine into a governed, security-conscious enterprise deployment pattern.
